name: Highway
rule: Open road, often blocked by wrecks and abandoned cars. Travel is 3 miles per hour on foot, or much faster by vehicle; a road is also where hordes drift.

name: Farmland
rule: Fields, fences, and farm buildings. Travel is 2 miles per hour on foot; forage is possible in season, and barns make good shelter.

name: Suburbs
rule: Street after street of houses and fences. Travel is 2 miles per hour; every house is a possible site and every corner a possible ambush.

name: City
rule: Dense streets, towers, and rubble. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; noise carries and the dead gather. Sites are rich and dangerous.

name: Forest
rule: Woodland, overgrown since the fall. Travel is 1.5 to 2 miles per hour; cover is good, forage is possible, and sightlines are short.

name: Hills
rule: Rolling or broken high ground. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour; a ridge gives a view and makes a bad place to be seen on.

name: Water
rule: Rivers, lakes, and coast. A boat makes about 4 miles per hour; swimming is slow and dangerous, and water is both a barrier and a supply.

name: Ruins
rule: Burned or collapsed ground. Travel is 1.5 miles per hour, and rubble hides site entrances and the dead.

name: Industrial Belt
rule: Warehouses, rail yards, and plants. Travel is 2 miles per hour; the buildings are large sites, and machines can be loud.
